text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages with six altered-quote variants each, for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Between March 2021 and September 2022, the Ndoro Valley Home Care Initiative trained 46 volunteer caregivers who conducted 3,180 home visits to adults living with HIV. Clients receiving at least two visits per month reported missed antiretroviral doses less often than clients visited monthly, and viral suppression among enrolled clients rose from 61% to 78%. The evaluation team did not find evidence that volunteers were overloaded, although caregivers in Kisaru ward covered twice the average number of households. Gloves were supplied consistently in all nine wards, but soap was not. Supervisors noted that referral forms were not always returned by the district clinic, which limited follow-up. Overall, the programme remains on track to meet its end-line targets, but caregiver stipends should be reviewed before the second phase begins.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Lumeta District Community Health Partnership deployed 212 community health workers across 38 villages, supported by your grant of $145,000. Each worker visited an average of 27 households per month, screening children under five for malnutrition and referring pregnant women for antenatal care. Facility deliveries rose to 71% of recorded births, up from 58% in the baseline year. We did not meet our target for tuberculosis case finding, largely because sputum transport from the northern villages was not funded until October. Mobile reporting worked in the lowland villages but not in the highland ones, where network coverage remained weak. Allowances were paid on time in the first half of the year but not in the second, yet only nine workers left the programme.

passages.source_passage: During the reporting period of January to June 2024, the Harrowgate Paralegal Outreach Service held 64 legal clinics in markets and community halls across Benwick County. Paralegals registered 1,027 new cases, of which 43% concerned land and inheritance disputes. Women made up roughly two thirds of clients, although men were the majority of clients seeking help with employment claims. Most cases were resolved not through the courts but through mediation, and the average time to resolution fell to 19 days. The service did not open its planned office in Tarrow because the lease was delayed. Paralegals referred 88 cases to partner advocates, but the advocates accepted only 51 of them owing to capacity limits.

passages.source_passage: Smallholder farmers in the Kesra Highlands cultivate an average of 1.4 hectares, mostly maize intercropped with beans. Since 2019, the Green Furrow Farmer Field School Network has grown from 12 to 57 schools, each meeting weekly through the growing season. Members who attended at least 80% of sessions harvested more maize per hectare than non-members in the same villages. Post-harvest losses in the area are not caused mainly by rodents but by weevils, and the network has no storage budget. Field facilitators are trained in soil fertility but not in pest management, which leaves a critical gap. Women lead 23 of the schools, yet they receive credit less often than men. The proposed project will address storage and pest control over three years.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Little Acorns Playgroup Network aimed to open 30 community playgroups by the end of 2024. As of 30 September, 26 playgroups are running, serving 412 children aged two to five. Attendance averaged 74% across the quarter, with the highest rates in Millbrook and the lowest in Fennick Cross. We have secured a venue in Ashby Lane but not in Hollins Park, so the Hollins group will not open before January. Parent volunteers lead most sessions; trained facilitators visit each group fortnightly and are not replacing volunteers but supporting them. A recent survey found that parents value the reading corner more than the outdoor play area. Spending is within budget, although transport costs rose by 12% after the fuel price increase.

passages.source_passage: The Sorrel Bay Community Counselling Service was founded in 2016 to respond to rising distress among fishing households after two consecutive seasons of poor catches. A 2022 household survey by the service found that one in four adults reported symptoms consistent with moderate depression, yet fewer than 10% had ever spoken to a health worker about their mood. Stigma was cited as a barrier by men but not by women; travel costs and long clinic queues deterred both. Help-seeking did not increase after the radio campaign, although awareness did. Our lay counsellors deliver group sessions in seven coastal villages, but individual sessions are not available outside the town centre. Men are referred by fishing cooperatives far less often than women are referred by church groups.

variants.moved_negation: Stigma was cited as a barrier not by men but by women; travel costs and long clinic queues deterred both.
variants.moved_negation_2: Help-seeking did increase after the radio campaign, although awareness did not.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023–24 project year, the Tamberi Rural Water Trust drilled 14 new boreholes and rehabilitated nine others across Okolo and Wendu sub-counties, bringing safe water within 500 metres of an estimated 6,800 residents. Household latrine coverage in target villages increased from 39% to 62%. Water quality tests at every new borehole met national standards, and no samples showed faecal contamination. Two boreholes in Wendu were capped not because of contamination but because of low yield. Water committees collected user fees in Okolo but not in Wendu, where committees are still being formed. Handwashing stations were installed at all 11 primary schools, though soap was supplied by the district in term one but not in term two.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the 2024 school year for the Puente Azul Scholarship Programme in the department of San Ilario. The programme supported 340 girls in lower and upper secondary school, covering fees, uniforms and a monthly transport stipend of 250 pesos. Attendance among scholars averaged 91%, compared with 79% among non-scholar classmates. Seventeen scholars withdrew during the year; none cited fees as the reason. Mentoring sessions were held monthly in urban schools but not in rural ones, because mentors could not travel during the rainy season. Scholars outperformed classmates in mathematics, while classmates outperformed scholars in language. Stipend payments were made on time in March but not in August, when the bank changed systems.

passages.source_passage: During 2023, the Dry Plains Resilience Project distributed seed of drought-tolerant sorghum and cowpea to 2,450 households in the Marula and Kepti districts. Rainfall was 35% below the long-term average, and the main rains arrived nearly four weeks late. Despite this, participating farmers harvested sorghum on 82% of planted plots, whereas many neighbouring maize fields failed entirely. Cowpea performed well on sandy soils but not on clay soils, where waterlogging after the late storms damaged seedlings. Community seed banks were established in 16 villages against a target of 20; the shortfall was not due to farmer interest but to a lack of secure storage. Farmers now prefer sorghum to maize for the short season, and demand for cowpea seed exceeds supply.

variants.changed_quantity_2: Rainfall was 35% below the long-term average, and the main rains arrived nearly six weeks late.

passages.source_passage: This update covers the Bramblegate Family Tracing and Foster Care Service for the quarter ending 31 March 2025. We currently support 58 children in foster placements with 41 approved carer families. Tracing caseworkers located relatives for 19 children, and 12 of those children were reunified after home assessments. Of those 12, five reunifications were delayed not by court dates but by home assessment backlogs. Placement breakdowns fell to three, compared with seven in the previous quarter. Carer recruitment has been strong in Hollow Reach but not in Dunmere, where we have only two approved families. The new case management system is used by caseworkers but not by foster carers. We ask the board to approve an additional recruitment officer for Dunmere and a part-time data clerk for Hollow Reach.
